posts.title: CIRIA 108 is still current on paper. TWf is now asking whether it still covers the mix you are pouring.
posts.excerpt: At the Temporary Works Forum 67th quarterly meeting at ICE on 9 September 2026, Andrew Jones of RMD Kwikform reported that work has started to calibrate CIRIA Report 108 Concrete pressure on formwork for current mixes. CIRIA 108 (1985) remains the industry calculation method most UK formwork and falsework designers still use. TWf and CIRIA have held initial meetings. Next steps are a working group, a project brief, funding, then industry consultation, testing and data collection. Until that work is issued, treat 108 as a method that must be justified against the actual mix, pour rate, temperature and placing method. Self-compacting, low-heat and ultra-low carbon concretes can stay fluid longer than the 1985 data assumed.
posts.linkedinReady:
CIRIA Report 108 is still the method most UK sites use for concrete pressure on formwork. It is also a 1985 document. That gap is now on the Temporary Works Forum agenda.

At the TWf 67th quarterly meeting at ICE on 9 September 2026, Andrew Jones (RMD Kwikform) reported initial meetings with CIRIA to calibrate Report 108 for current mixes. A working group, project brief, funding and industry testing are the next steps. That is not a new design standard. It is an admission that rate of rise, temperature and concrete grouping in 108 were built around mixes that are no longer the default pour.

For the TWC and TWS: put every wall, column, core and shaft pour on the Temporary Works Register. The design brief must state mix type, slump or flow, admixtures, pour rate, pour height, concrete temperature, pump method and whether the pour is top-down or bottom-up. Do not apply a 108 envelope to self-compacting or low-heat concrete without the designer stating why the 1985 grouping still applies. Hold permit to pour until formwork, ties, walings and pour rate are as designed. A faster pour than the brief is a changed load case.

Educational only. Not for construction. Subject to the project temporary works procedure.

body.p: The Temporary Works Forum held its 67th quarterly meeting at the Institution of Civil Engineers, One Great George Street, on Wednesday 9 September 2026. TWf's public meeting note records that Rob Millard opened the session, nine new member organisations had joined since the June meeting, and Andrew Jones of RMD Kwikform presented Calibrating CIRIA Report 108 for the Current Age. Jones reported that initial meetings had taken place over the summer, including engagement with CIRIA. Next steps included formation of a working group, a project brief and funding, then industry-wide consultation, testing and data collection. CIRIA Report 108, Concrete pressure on formwork, was published in 1985 and remains listed as current.

Formwork pressure is a temporary works load case with collapse consequence to people working below and beside the pour. CIRIA 108 gives Pmax as the lesser of a rate-of-rise expression and full hydrostatic head. Coefficients were calibrated on data that predates widespread self-compacting, low-heat and ultra-low carbon mixes. Until revised guidance is published, 108 is still the available method. It is not an automatic envelope. Standard does not automatically mean low risk. Provisional category only - to be confirmed by the TWC and the project temporary works procedure.

body.h: Practical TWC and TWS control points
ul: Register every formwork, falsework, climbing form, shaft lining and single-sided wall pour on the Temporary Works Register before the first concrete is ordered.

Write a design brief that states mix type and grouping, slump or flow class, admixtures, target pour rate and pour height, concrete temperature, pump line arrangement and whether placing is from the top or the base.

Require the designer to state whether CIRIA 108 is being used as a screening check or as the design envelope, and why the 1985 grouping still applies to this mix. If it does not, design for hydrostatic pressure or for a project-specific justification.
Do not treat a faster pour, a warmer day, a delayed lift or a change from skip to pump as the same load case.

Hold permit to pour until formwork is inspected against the drawing, pour rate is agreed with the supplier, and the TWS or appointed inspector has signed the check. Stop the pour if the rate of rise exceeds the brief.
Independent check category is provisional only. Tall walls, single-sided forms, public interface, SCC or low-heat mixes normally point to escalation, not a CAT 0 close-out.

body.p: Educational briefing only. Not for construction. Not a design, not a check and not a permit. Subject to project-specific verification of mix data, pour rate, temperature, formwork system, tie capacity, sequence and responsible persons, and to acceptance under the project temporary works procedure. Exact clause references in CIRIA Report 108, BS 5975-1:2024, BS 5975-2:2024 and BS EN 12812 are to be confirmed against the project's licensed copies. AI-assisted drafting requires competent review before use on site. Do not proceed until reviewed and accepted by the competent person under the project temporary works procedure.

posts.title: Woodbridge trench collapse: director jailed after excavation undermined a conservatory
posts.excerpt: On 15 September 2026 Ipswich Crown Court sentenced Peter Clifford, former director of Hintonwood East Anglia Ltd, to eight years and 10 months after Dale Baker, 30, suffocated in a trench collapse at Haughgate Close, Woodbridge on 15 December 2020. Police and the joint HSE investigation found the trench had been dug next to a conservatory with no adequate shuttering and no support to the existing foundations. The company admitted Health and Safety at Work Act offences. A domestic extension trench is still a temporary works item. Undermining existing structure is a second collapse mechanism, not a footnote.
